taxonomy:
Below is a taxonomy of **grid-based logic games** based strictly on the *types of objects/actions and constraints* described in the provided rules (e.g., place bulbs, draw bridges, shade cells, draw loops, connect dots, move circles, fill numbers, divide into regions/blocks).

---

## 1) Illumination / Visibility games
Games where the core action is **placing lights** so that squares become illuminated under blocking/obstacle constraints.

- **Akari**  
  Place light bulbs in white squares. Bulbs illuminate in row/column until black squares/frame. Every white square must be illuminated; bulbs must not illuminate other bulbs.

---

## 2) Rectangle / region partitioning & region-size games
Games where the main task is to **partition the grid into rectangles/rooms/blocks/tiles** using given numbers.

- **Shikaku**  
  Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its cell count.
- **Chained Block**  
  Partition into black “blocks”; each block has a specified size (or “?”). All blocks must form a chain with shape/size uniqueness constraints.
- **Choco Banana**  
  Paint some cells black so black connected components form rectangles/squares; white connectedness must avoid forming rectangles/squares; numbers constrain area size.
- **Heyawake**  
  Rooms by bold borders; each room has a number of painted cells; white/pained connectivity constraints across rooms.
- **Nurimeizu**  
  Rooms enclosed by bold lines; each room has exactly two same-sized blocks of equal number-of-cells (shapes), blocks connected and not touching each other.
- **Ripple Effect**  
  “Rooms” by bold lines; each room contains consecutive numbers starting from 1; duplication distance constraints within rows/columns.
- **Moon-or-Sun**  
  Rooms by bold borders; loop passes each room once; per-room constraint: loop goes through either all moon cells or all sun cells.

---

## 3) Shading / coloring (black-white) with connectivity and local shape rules
Games primarily defined by **coloring cells** black/white (or shading), with global connectivity and local structural constraints.

- **Choco Banana** (paint some cells black; linked black cells form rectangles/squares; linked white cells must not form rectangle/square)
- **Hitori** (black cells do not touch side-to-side; no duplicate numbers in any row/column among unhidden/white cells; white cells form continuous network)
- **Kurodoko** (color cells black; numbered cells forced white; black cells don’t touch side-to-side; all white cells connected)
- **Kurotto** (cells colored with circle constraints; circle cells cannot be colored; circle number = sum of continuous black lengths in four directions)
- **LITS** (color tetrominoes inside bold areas; similarly-shaped tetrominoes can’t touch except corners; colored squares connected; no 2×2 or larger colored squares)
- **Nuritwin** (shade some cells; each outlined region has exactly two blocks of same number size; shaded blocks connected; two blocks in region can’t touch side-to-side; no fully shaded 2×2)
- **Nurikabe** (fill with white regions constrained by numbers; black cells form continuous wall and cannot form 2×2; numbered cells are white region identifiers)
- **Sto-stone** (drop stones by gravity into bottom half with room constraints on continuous black cell counts; black cannot connect across bold lines; final configuration connectivity by drop constraints)
- **Usowan** (colored cells have adjacency count constraints; number indicates colored neighbors; exactly one wrong number per bold rectangle; colored cells can’t touch side-to-side; white not separated by colored)

---

## 4) Loop-drawing games (single non-self-crossing loop)
Games where the primary object is a **single loop** drawn through cell centers/edges with restrictions.

- **Dotchi-Loop**  
  Single loop through cell centers; must pass all white circles; in each bold-enclosed area, loop goes straight through all white circles or turns right at all of them; must not pass black circles.
- **Masyu**  
  Single loop through centers; passes all circles; white circle forces straight-through and at least one right turn next to it; black circle forces right turn and then straight through next cell.
- **Nagareru**  
  Single continuous loop in direction; passes through arrow cells; wind constraints prevent moving against wind and enforce minimum step in wind-blow direction when entering wind from side.
- **Mid-loop**  
  Single loop through cell centers; must pass all black circles with circle as midpoint of straight segment.
- **Moon-or-Sun**  
  Loop goes through each bold room once; per-room all moon or all sun; cannot mix types within a room; order alternates room-by-room (moons then suns then moons...).
- **Suraromu**  
  Single loop passing through all “gates” (dotted lines); start/end at open numbered circle; gate numbers constrain crossing order; gates can only be passed once.
- **Yajilin**  
  Single loop through cell centers; does not pass through black cells or numbered cells; black cells can’t touch side-to-side.
- **Slitherlink**  
  Loop on dotted grid: single loop connecting dots with line-count numbers indicating how many surrounding edges belong to the loop; empty cells allow any.

---

## 5) Path/connection (non-loop) games using lines between cells/dots
Games where the main action is **connecting pairs or drawing paths** rather than a loop.

- **Numberlink**  
  Connect pairs of identical numbers with a continuous non-branching path through centers; cannot cross or go through numbered cells improperly.
- **Hashiwokakero**  
  Connect islands with bridges (number of bridges equals island number); max two bridges between islands; bridges can’t cross islands/bridges; all islands become continuously linked.
- **Hebi**  
  Place sequential snake parts 1→5 in white squares; snakes can’t touch side-to-side; visibility/tail constraints relative to arrows and black squares.
- **Satogaeri**  
  Move circles horizontally/vertically within track-like constraints so each country has one circle; numbers in circles constrain how many cells they pass through; circles can’t cross tracks or other circles.
- **Yosenabe**  
  Move all circles into gray areas; each circle movement shown by straight arrows (no bending); cannot cross other circles/arrows; gray-area sum of entering circle numbers must match required sum.

---

## 6) Numerical filling / Sudoku-style constraint satisfaction
Games where the key action is to **place numbers** satisfying row/column (or grid-block) rules.

- **Sudoku**  
  Place numbers 1–9 so each row, column, and bold 3×3 block contains all numbers 1–9.
- **Nansuke**  
  Fill blanks with given digits from a list; each cell has exactly one digit; digits correspond to up/down or left/right directions.
- **Juosan**  
  Fill all cells with either “—” or “|”; bold-enclosed territories have required counts; extend limits differ horizontally/vertically and for each mark type.
- **Fillomino**  
  Fill all empty cells with numbers; form blocks of same number size; same-sized blocks can’t touch side-to-side.
- **Ripple Effect**  
  (Also fits region-numbering) Each room has consecutive numbers starting from 1 with duplicate-distance constraints.

---

## 7) Arrow-constrained “growth” / directional placement games
Games that define movement/growth via **arrows** and “directional progress”.

- **Evolomino**  
  Fill in each pre-defined block/arrows with rule that arrows indicate growth of blocks by adding squares without rotation/flipping (progressive construction).
- **Pencils**  
  Place straight pencil lines from a tip through cells with turning allowed; numbers indicate pencil length; lines can’t cross or branch; pencil shape is a straight polyline.
- **Nagareru**  
  (Also loop-based) Wind direction from arrows constrains movement of loop.
- **Yajilin** / **Suraromu** / **Dotchi-Loop**  
  (Also loop-based) but include arrow/number constraints in gate/circle interactions; included more broadly above.

---

## 8) Polyomino/tile placement games with adjacency rules
Games where shapes (tetrominoes/blocks) must be placed/filled under shape-interaction constraints.

- **Evolomino**  
  Block growth via adding squares step-by-step along arrow route with no rotation/flip.
- **LITS**  
  Place tetrominoes (4-cell shapes) inside bold areas; similarly shaped rotated/reversed tetrominoes can’t touch (except corners); colored squares connected; no large squares.
- **Nurimeizu / Nuritwin**  
  (Also region-based) enforce block shapes via cell counts and block connectivity, though not necessarily named polyominoes.

---

## 9) Block/cluster (“island”, “territory”, “room”) chain/link structure games
Games emphasizing that **all pieces must belong to a global chain/network** with restrictions.

- **Chained Block**  
  All blocks must be part of a chain; chain formed when blocks contact at corners; uniqueness of block shapes in chain.
- **Hashiwokakero**  
  Bridges form a continuous link between all islands.
- **Hitori** / **Kurodoko** / **Nurimeizu** / **Nuritwin**  
  Include connectivity requirements (white cell continuous; blocks connected; overall constraints that shaded/white structures become linked).

---

# Summary of taxonomy mapping (quick index)
- **Illumination:** Akari  
- **Region partition/rectangle constraints:** Shikaku, Chained Block, Choco Banana (area constraints), Heyawake, Nurimeizu, Ripple Effect, Moon-or-Sun  
- **Shading/coloring (black-white):** Hitori, Kurodoko, Kurotto, LITS, Nuritwin, Nurikabe, Sto-stone, Usowan, Choco Banana  
- **Single loops:** Dotchi-Loop, Masyu, Nagareru, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun, Suraromu, Yajilin, Slitherlink  
- **Connections/paths/bridges/movement lines:** Numberlink, Hashiwokakero, Hebi, Satogaeri, Yosenabe  
- **Pure number filling:** Sudoku, Nansuke, Juosan, Fillomino  
- **Arrow-directional construction:** Evolomino, Pencils, Nagareru  
- **Shape placement:** LITS, Evolomino (shape growth), Nurimeizu/Nuritwin (block shapes by counts)
